thread:
ana: Quick UX/design question about how we pick samples for regression diffs in eval runs. Current behavior shows first 3 outputs per prompt. Users reported noisy results and want more "representative" sampling. Thoughts?
ralph: From infra/eng side, we can surface sampling mode: first, random, worst-case (by score), and stratified (by bucket). Costs: worst-case requires pre-scoring which is extra step.
jas: UX opinon: expose a compact dropdown with labels: 'First', 'Random', 'Top regressions', 'Representative'. Keep default as 'Representative' (stratified) for broader coverage.
mira: copy nit: 'Top regressions' sounds scary. Maybe 'Highest delta' or 'Worst regressions' but need to be clear for non-ML folks. Also add a tooltip explaining what each means.
ralph: agree on tooltip. Implementation note: 'Representative' = sample across score quartiles by default (1 per quartile) so it surfaces edge cases and central tendency. That seems reasonable.
a11y-bot: a11y note: sampling dropdown must be keyboard accessible and the tooltip should be accessible via aria-describedby. If we auto-update the samples on change, announce with aria-live="polite": 'Samples updated: 4 previews'.
jas: UI placement thought: put sampling selector next to the 'Run summary' header. On narrow screens collapse into an overflow menu. Also persist choice per user.
nana: microcopy options for tooltip for 'Representative': 1) 'Selects samples across score ranges to show diverse outputs.' 2) 'Shows examples from low to high scoring outputs.' Which is clearer?
mira: prefer option 1, but shorter: 'Picks examples across score ranges for diversity.'
ralph: backend question: do we precompute quartiles at run-time? if runs are huge it might be heavier. maybe compute approximate quantiles on shard and merge. We can add a flag to make it async and show a loading spinner in the sample tiles.
jas: UX for loading: show skeleton cards with 'Computing samples...' and a small progress spinner. Also provide a fallback to 'Random' if compute exceeds 3s.
qa-bot: Test tasks created: 'sample-selection-modes', 'sample-loading-fallback', 'sample-dropdown-keyboard-announce'.
mira: another related item: scorecard legend is confusing. People ask whether green means 'passed threshold' or 'higher score is better'. Proposal: change legend to 'Pass / Marginal / Fail' with thresholds and a hover explainer.
ja s: +1. Also add textual label on small chips: instead of only color dot, show 'Pass' or 'Fail' inside the chip for compact mode. Helps colorblind folks.
a11y-bot: confirm: chips must have visible text or at least sr-only text. Color alone is insufficient. Also ensure contrast ratio for chip text meets 4.5:1.
ralph: will adjust tokens. We'll make 'Pass' chip dark green with white text, 'Marginal' amber with black text, 'Fail' red with white text.
nana: tiny copy tweak for CTA: change 'View samples' -> 'Open samples' in places where it opens the modal, keep 'View' where it just expands inline.
mira: good UX distinction. Action items: 1) add sampling selector (First/Random/Representative/Highest delta) with accessible tooltips 2) default 'Representative' with approx quartile sampling, async compute + skeletons + fallback 3) persist user choice 4) update scorecard legend to explicit Pass/Marginal/Fail labels and chips with readable text 5) QA tests for keyboard and loading.
jas: I'll mock screens and put variants in Figma; will add copy for tooltips.
ralph: I'll prototype approximate quantile job + fallback and add API to return sample mode metadata. ETA: next week.
nana: I'll run quick content poll on the tooltip phrasing and post results here.
mira: thanks all. tagging the PR & QA tasks here when up. :seedling:
